title: Cold sores: how to get antiviral pills prescribed through your AI

## Why does having the same doctor matter for cold sores?


Because the herpes simplex virus stays in the body for life, cold sores return over time. Staying with the same doctor in one ongoing chat thread lets you build trust, test treatments together, and track progress. Your physician can also prescribe an on-hand course of valacyclovir or famciclovir for the next outbreak's first tingle, if your doctor decides it's right for you. Ahead of dental work, lip fillers, or laser procedures, you can ask that same doctor whether preventive dosing makes sense ([AAD](https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/a-z/cold-sores-self-care) ). If outbreaks reach six or more a year, you can decide together whether to try daily suppression, and when to step back down.


Your doctor's only incentive is helping you. ## AI cold sore treatment: why timing matters for antiviral pills


Cold sores, also known as fever blisters or herpes simplex labialis, form around the lips and stay contagious until completely scabbed ([AAD](https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/a-z/cold-sores-overview) ). Roughly 60% of American adults carry HSV-1 ([NIDCR](https://www.nidcr.nih.gov/health-info/fever-blisters-canker-sores) ), a nerve-dwelling virus reactivated by sunlight, stress, fatigue, illness, menstrual periods, or dental work ([AAD](https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/a-z/cold-sores-causes) ). Episodes typically begin with localized tingling, burning, or itching before fluid-filled blisters appear, crust over, and in healthy people most heal in 5 to 15 days ([AAD](https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/a-z/cold-sores-symptoms) ).


Published labels and trials show why early dosing matters:


-


**Valacyclovir (Valtrex):** Approved from age 12 as two 2-gram doses taken 12 hours apart on one day at the first warning sign ([DailyMed](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=valacyclovir) ). In two trials (1,856 people), episodes averaged about one day shorter than placebo; benefit is not shown once blisters form.


-


**Famciclovir:** Approved for immunocompetent adults with recurrent cold sores as one 1,500 mg dose taken when warning symptoms start ([DailyMed](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=famciclovir) ). In its trial, dosing within one hour cut median healing time to 4.4 days versus 6.2 on placebo and median pain to 1.7 versus 2.9 days.


-


**Oral acyclovir tablets:** Prescribed off-label when treating oral cold sores ([DailyMed](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=acyclovir) ). In a[1990 trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2153735/) (400 mg five times daily for five days), earliest-stage starters had 36% shorter pain and 27% faster healing on average, while a[2026 Cochrane review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42813499/) (87 trials, 22,631 people) found valacyclovir shortened healing by about one day on average and oral acyclovir showed little or no difference in one small trial.


If you prefer creams, non-prescription docosanol 10% ([Abreva](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=docosanol) ) is applied five times daily from the first tingle for ages 12 and older, while prescription acyclovir 5% (Zovirax) and penciclovir 1% ([Denavir](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=penciclovir) ) cut healing time by roughly half a day to one day on average.


## How does a FutureClinic visit compare with an office visit?


If you need an in-person procedure, a local office suits you better. When you only need a cold sore evaluation,[AMN Healthcare's May 2025 survey](https://ir.amnhealthcare.com/2025-05-27-New-Survey-Shows-Physician-Appointment-Wait-Times-Surge-19-Since-2022,-48-Since-2004) across 15 US metros found new-patient waits averaging 36.5 days for dermatology and 23.5 days for family medicine, while an[American Journal of Managed Care study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26295356/) reported an average visit takes 121 minutes (37 minutes traveling and 84 minutes on site). At FutureClinic, we believe AI is a tool for doctors, with the doctor in charge: only a medical expert can catch an AI mistake, so our AI works behind the scenes like a chief resident preparing your case, and never gives medical advice by itself.
